title: Simple module
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ an $R$-module. $M$ is *simple* if $M\ne0$ and every $R$-submodule of $M$ is either $0$ or $M$.

mathlib_searches.query: simple module: nonzero module whose only submodules are zero and itself
simple module over a ring: submodule lattice has exactly two elements

mathlib_searches.results: RingTheory/SimpleModule/Basic.lean:60 class IsSimpleModule extends IsSimpleOrder (Submodule R M); Order/Atoms.lean:733 class IsSimpleOrder extends Nontrivial α with eq_bot_or_eq_top : ∀ a, a = ⊥ ∨ a = ⊤

mathlib_match.how: exact: IsSimpleModule R M is IsSimpleOrder (Submodule R M), i.e. the submodule lattice is nontrivial (⊥ ≠ ⊤, so M ≠ 0) and every submodule is ⊥ or ⊤. Mathlib allows any ring R.

note: Not the same notion as def-wf-simple-module (simple modules of an algebraic group, stable subspaces), which is why a separate node is created.
